posts.text:
$197.3 million is headed to Oregon’s rural hospitals in 2027!

The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services has awarded $197.3 million for fiscal year 2027 to improve and modernize rural health care in Oregon, building on last year’s $197.3 million.

I am proud to be the only

“Veterans know better than anyone else the price of freedom, for they’ve suffered the scars of war. We can offer them no better tribute than to protect what they have won for us.” – President Ronald Reagan.

This Veterans Day, please take a moment to remember what veterans have https://t.co/JASVmInWSu

Wednesday of last week, I had a great discussion with Bill Meyer in KMED’s Medford studio. We talked about the importance of voter turnout, the change we need to see in the Oregon governor’s office, and the importance of passing my Wildfire Reduction Market Expansion Act, which

As do all parents, I carry with me the constant and dreadful fear that my children may be harmed or injured. When something horrific and horrible happens to someone else’s children, as is the awful fact at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, I am outraged and deeply saddened. Our deepest, deepest, sympathies are extended to the families of the children who lost their lives, and to the family of the teacher who was killed. We pray for the recovery of those who were injured, and we say thank you—thank you—to the courageous citizen who took immediate action to defend the innocent from certain death.

There are resources available to help those who are suffering from the mental distress of these tragedies. For the local crisis line, call 541-322-7500 extension 9.

Wolf attacks on cattle cost ranchers about $130 million every single year across the United States. Each of these attacks trigger chronic stress and diminish birth rates among cattle. And while gray wolves remain on the endangered species list, there is nothing that ranchers can do to protect their herds.

Please see the attached article to learn more about my push to delist the gray wolf.
https://t.co/1p57Dgc9Qw

It was a real pleasure to work with Kingsley Field and the Department of the Air Force to deliver formal authorization to convert Kingsley Field to a F-35A Lightning II training base.

Please see the attached article to learn more about the work my office and I have done to make this happen!

https://t.co/aNRfG8diiz

As a senior member of the Natural Resources Committee, I am working to ensure environmental groups are following the law and to hold them accountable.

I’m pleased to report that the Natural Resources Committee has opened an investigation into 19 environmental groups, including Oregon Wild and Cascadia Wildlands, to determine if they are weaponizing litigation and abusing the law to profit from taxpayers.

Please see the attached article to learn more about the investigation.

https://t.co/PRlLl4ABuR

A significant portion of the homeless and prison population suffer from severe mental illness. These people would benefit from the availability of proper treatment in our existing mental healthcare facilities.

That is why I introduced the IMD CARE Act today. This bill would result in an increased number of beds and treatment available for mentally ill people.

Without this improvement in how we deliver mental health services, those who need such treatment will continue to cost communities more in law enforcement and healthcare expenses. The circular progression of the mentally ill from the street to the hospital to the prison and back to the street must stop.

See the press release on my website below!

https://t.co/UxmMPz7tTx

I am very pleased to announce that the Wallowa Memorial Hospital was selected to receive a $5.46 million grant from the Big Beautiful Bill. This federal investment in Wallowa County means that county residents will be able to obtain high-quality medical assistance much more quickly and much more closely to home. This is exactly one of the many positive outcomes I hoped for when I voted for the Big Beautiful Bill.

https://t.co/SxXiGhXgrP

Today marks 25 years since the attacks on the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and the attempted attack that ended in the fields of Shanksville Pennsylvania on September 11, 2001. 

We will always remember the tragedy of the 2977 men and women who lost their lives; we will always remember the bravery of the American heroes who ran toward danger; and we will always remember the responsibility to protect what is most sacred against those that wish for America’s destruction. 

We will never forget.

Thanks to everyone who attended my wildfire townhalls - we had lots of productive conversation.

https://t.co/xf4QGiRcCX

REMINDER KLAMATH COUNTY:

U.S. Congressman Cliff Bentz will host another town hall TODAY focused on recent wildfires in Klamath County.

It will take place later this morning, 10 AM, at the Klamath County Fairgrounds Hall #2, 3531 S 6th St., Klamath Falls, OR, 97603.

It’s always great to stop by KMED’s studio with Bill Meyer. We had an excellent discussion on the Fix Our Forest Act (which has passed the House), my Fire Townhalls across the district, and my meetings across southern Oregon. https://t.co/CRZvBJm07y
It was great to visit the KOBI studio in Medford where I gave an update on my wildfire meetings across the district. https://t.co/FUo4TP2R1R

Good news! I just received word from Tootie Smith, State Executive Director of the USDA Farm Service Agency, that Oregon has now been approved to utilize Conservation Reserve Programs (CRP) lands for emergency grazing due to the catastrophic wildfires burning through my district. This decision should be of some help to alleviate the burden our ranchers are facing to find grazing land for their cattle.  

Please contact your local Farm Service Agency for details.
Yesterday, FEMA authorized use of federal funds to help Oregon fight the Fox Fire and the Rowe Creek Complex. These funds will help reimburse Oregon for firefighting costs.

Please see the attached story about my recently introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reducing the danger of cataclysmic wildfire.

https://t.co/JcEuoS5FE6

Happy 250th Birthday America!

Today we might take a moment to remember that this day of celebration is possible only because of the genius of our founders, the sacrifices made by veterans, and the work of everyday Americans to keep our economy, our schools, and our many levels of government working.

God bless each of you and this great country!!!

Congratulations to Yi-jia (Lyra Lu), a student from Burns High School in Oregon’s Second Congressional District for winning this year’s Congressional Art Competition with her outstanding piece, “Still, She Rises.”

Her artwork will be proudly displayed in the U.S. Capitol for the next year, alongside the winning entries from across the country. It was a pleasure to meet Yi-jia (Lyra Lu) here in Washington, D.C.!

Today, the @NatResources Committee, on which I serve, advanced the Great American Outdoors Act 250 to help address the maintenance backlog on our public lands, improve access for the people who use them, and ensure these lands remain available for future generations.

Good stewardship begins with taking care of the assets we already have. By investing in needed repairs and infrastructure, we can better support recreation, public access, and responsible management of America’s public lands. #GAOA250
https://t.co/3VcLpE4OuJ

Hydropower is one of our nation's most reliable, affordable, and clean energy sources, but outdated licensing requirements and endless litigation are putting many projects at risk.
 
That's why I introduced the Hydropower Licensing Affordability Act, legislation that brings greater clarity and accountability to the federal licensing process while ensuring mitigation requirements are reasonable and tied to a project's actual impacts.
 
As energy demand continues to grow, we must protect and strengthen the hydropower resources that help keep electricity affordable and reliable for families and businesses across Oregon and the nation.

Protecting our forests, strengthening consumer privacy, supporting agriculture, and addressing national security challenges remain top priorities.

Read more about my recent work in Congress and the issues impacting Oregon’s Second Congressional District. ⬇️

https://t.co/OriAJ3HGag

Happy 251st birthday to the U.S. Army! 

Thank you to the brave men and women who valiantly serve and have served. Our nation would not be what it is without you. https://t.co/N9TzNwfNP5

Today, I attended a House Natural Resources Committee Committee hearing on The Great American Outdoors Act 250, held in Hot Springs, Arkansas.  

I’d like to thank Chairman Bruce Westerman for holding the hearing where we examined legislation aimed at enhancing public lands access, improving infrastructure, and creating new outdoor recreation opportunities in our nation’s crown jewels like Crater Lake National Park, and in this case, Hot Springs National Park.  

I’d also like to thank my Democrat colleges from Oregon, both Congresswoman Val Hoyle and Congresswoman Maxine Dexter for also attending the hearing.  

Among our witnesses was actor Kevin Costner who shared his personal stories about the importance of getting outdoors and recognizing this history of our Country’s natural resources.  

We also had Department of Interior Deputy Secretary Kate McGregor testify about the Administration’s work with Congress to maximize the experience for those to visit our National Parks and National Forests.  

It was great fun!

It was great meeting with students from the Pendleton FFA Chapter from Pendleton High School.

FFA programs provide students with valuable hands on learning experiences and leadership opportunities that help prepare the next generation of Oregon’s agricultural community. I know that Oregon agriculture has a bright future, and these students are helping lead the way!

It was a pleasure meeting with Makeena, a student from South Umpqua High School in Myrtle Creek, Oregon. Congratulations to her on being recognized as a recipient of the 2026 Capitol Hill Challenge Award. 

We also spoke about my journey to Congress, public service, and the growing opportunities available to young people interested in government.

A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
